Furthermore, this combiner is used for not only power combination but also impedance matching between its input and output ports by selecting a suitable coupling coefficient. The size of the 2-way power combiner used here is 84× 300$\mu \mathrm{m}^{2}$, and the size of the entire PA is 2.5 m$\mathrm{m}^{2}$. The power density per chip area is 364 mW/m$\mathrm{m}^{2}$, which is the second largest value reported in the literature. In addition, this PA achieves a large signal gain of 20 dB at the maximum output power, the highest reported value in the literature.

articleTitle: Design of a 22-55 GHz SPDT Switch MMIC with GaAs PIN Diodes
abstract: Design and measured performance of a mmWave reflective SPDT switch MMIC with vertical RF PIN diodes on GaAs are presented. The switch design uses a modified double shunt topology with distributed switching elements to extend the bandwidth beyond the limitations of the classic shunt topology. The bias feed and filtering network is integrated on-chip. The RF transitions are implemented with hot vias to a PCB to which the MMIC is mounted with silver epoxy. In the $22-55 \mathrm{GHz}$ frequency range, the measured insertion loss is less than $1 \mathrm{~dB}$, return loss is better than $15 \mathrm{~dB}$, and the isolation is greater than $40 \mathrm{~dB}$.

articleTitle: A 75-140 GHz Frequency Quadrupler with Milli-Watt Level Output Power in 22nm FDSOI
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-wideband frequency quadrupler formed of two polyphase frequency doublers sandwiching a balanced power amplifier. Quadrature phases are employed to suppress undesired harmonics that fall within the bands of interest. Implemented in 22nm FDSOI technology, the proposed quadrupler operates from 74 to 140 GHz, achieving 66 GHz bandwidth and 62% FBW, with a peak saturated output power of 4.8 dBm at 120 GHz. To the authors’ knowledge, the proposed design has the highest reported fractional bandwidth to date, compared to non-distributed CMOS and SiGe quadruplers, while delivering an output power above 0dBm and a harmonic suppression higher than 21 dB.

articleTitle: A Push-Pull 6–12GHz GaN Dual-Stage MMIC PA with Capacitive Cross-Coupling Neutralization for Increased Gain
abstract: This paper presents a $6-12\mathrm{GHz}\quad \mathrm{GaN}$ on SiC two-stage MMIC push-pull PA using Marchand baluns. The differential topology is used to implement capacitive cross-coupling neutralization to increase the amplifier gain. A methodology to create an accurate model of the neutralized transistor including the parasitics of the neutralization network is discussed. An octave bandwidth balun with amplitude and phase imbalances below $0.2\mathrm{~dB}$ and 2.5° is described. The MMIC PA is fully characterized and $26\mathrm{~dB}$ of small signal gain and a peak output power of 37.2dBm with a PAE of $ 30.5\%$ is measured at 7GHz.

articleTitle: A Ka-band CMOS Active Phase Shifter Using Active Balun for Phase optimization
abstract: In this paper, we designed a CMOS active phase shifter that operates in the Ka-band. In the active phase shifter, the differential signals with high phase accuracy were generated using active balun to alleviate complexity, thereby reducing the insertion loss of I/Q generator. In addition, we proposed a layout technique that can secure symmetry between the output signals of poly phase filter (PPF). To verify the feasibility of the proposed design technique, we designed an Ka-band active phase shifter using 65 nm RFCMOS process. The core size of the designed phase shifter was 0.506× 0.257m$\mathrm{m}^{2}$. At the target frequency of 28 GHz, the measured RMS phase and gain errors were lower than 0.35° and 0.07 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: A 182 GHz Triple-Stacked Distributed Amplifier in InP HBT Process
abstract: This paper presents a wideband distributed amplifier (DA) in an Indium Phosphide (InP) heterojunction bipolar transistor (HBT) process. The DA integrates eight gain cells, each designed with a triple-stacked topology to achieve high gain and output power. An emitter resistive-capacitive (RC) degeneration is incorporated within each gain cell to reach a broad bandwidth. Furthermore, each cell is equipped with a back-side-via, which facilitates immediate grounding for shunt elements. This feature enables the DA to maintain a flat gain and avoid potential instability issues. The $D A$ achieves an average gain of $12 \mathrm{~dB}$ with a $5 \mathrm{~dB}$ gain peaking at 165GHz compared to the gain at low frequency. The DA demonstrates a 3-dB bandwidth ranging from DC to 182GHz. It outputs a maximum saturated power $\left(P_{s a t}\right)$ of 14dBm and a peak output power at 1-dB compression point $\left(\mathrm{P}_{1 \mathrm{~dB}}\right)$ of 9.8dBm. Within the frequency spectrum of 1-170 GHz, the $D A$ delivers an average $P_{\text {sat }}$ of 12.2dBm.

articleTitle: A Fully-Differential Travelling-Wave Amplifier up to 110 GHz in a 22 nm FD-SOI CMOS Technology
abstract: This work presents a fully-differential travelling-wave amplifier (TWA) designed in a 22nm FD-SOI CMOS technology covering the entirely frequency range from 3 to 110 GHz. The amplifier reaches a peak differential gain of 13 dB at 10 GHz and 4 dB at 110 GHz. The amplifier is built by ten unit gain cells with a total power consumption of 278mW and is the first presented travelling-wave amplifier with a measured common mode rejection ration (CMRR) up to 95 GHz with a peak CMRR of 13 dB at 7 GHz.

articleTitle: Phase- and Amplitude Noise Suppression using a Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer
abstract: This paper describes the verification of the phase- and amplitude noise suppression property of a Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer (JAWS) circuit. Simulations are performed to gain insight in the improvement in signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) delivered by the JAWS circuit when random amplitude andjitter noise are introduced. Measurements show an improvement for both integrated phase- and amplitude noise of 15 to 40 dB for synthesized frequencies in the range of 0.5-2MHz.

articleTitle: A X4 Multiplier MMIC to E-Band Frequencies with High Spectral Purity in 50 nm mHEMT Technology
abstract: This paper presents a X4 frequency multiplier MMIC realized in the IAF 50 nm mHEMT technology. It consists of two cascaded frequency doublers followed by an amplifier and was designed for an output frequency range from 70 to 82.5 GHz. This corresponds to a bandwidth of 12.5 GHz or 16.4 %. The MMIC achieves a relatively flat output power of 9.5 dBm with a variation of only ± 0.4dB. The unwanted harmonics were suppressed in the output spectrum by more than 52 dBc.

articleTitle: Heterointegration of mm-Wave InP-HBT Power Amplifier Chiplets on SiGe-BiCMOS Chip
abstract: In this paper we demonstrate InP chiplet heterointegration on SiGe-BiCMOS carriers for mm-wave applications. A flip-chip type of assembly with indium-based microbumps allows for seamless integration with minimal losses up to more than 300 GHz. A single-stage InP-HBT power amplifier was used to highlight the functionality of the heterointegration approach.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a 50GHz InP DHBT Class-E Power Amplifier Providing 2.3 mW/µm2
abstract: For the commercial success of mm-wave 5G technologies, there is a need for high-output power and efficient power amplifier systems. In this paper, we demonstrate the capability of InP DHBT devices at the V band and achieve a high power density of $2.3\mathrm{~mW}/\mu\mathrm{m}^{2}$ at 50GHz. The simulated and measured class E is analysed and compared with an analytical HBT switching model. A single-stage, single-finger of $0.85\times 6\mu\mathrm{m}^{2}$ (emitter area) class E power amplifier is designed to reach this high power density with a PAE of 28.3%.

articleTitle: A 12 GS/s RF-Sampler Employing Inductive Peaking in 22 nm FD-SOI CMOS
abstract: This paper presents a 12 GS/s RF-sampler in 22nm FD-SOI CMOS. An RF-impedance matched FE-butter drives the proposed track-and-hold circuit. For the first time, inductive peaking is utilized inside a track-and-hold to increase the bandwidth over 23% from initially 12.9 GHz to 15.9 GHz compared to an un-peaked sampler without consuming additional power. No time-interleaving is utilized, eliminating the need for calibration of gain/offset/sample-phase mismatches. The RF-sampler maintains a SFDR and SNR above 53 dB and 49.8 dB, respectively, across the entire Nyquist band. A high frequency SNR improvement of 1.5 dB is simulated. The proposed RF-sampler is insensitive to input common-mode as well as supply voltage variations. The simulated clock jitter is only 22fs, which does not degrade the high-frequency SNR. A total power consumption of only 58 mW is required from a 1.2 V and 0.9 V supply.

articleTitle: A 39.5 dBm GaN Doherty Amplifier MMIC with Phase Control for Ka-band Space Applications
abstract: In this paper, a high-power multi-cell, multi-stage GaN MMIC Doherty Power Amplifier (DPA) for space applications is presented. The amplifier implements a novel approach for the Doherty output power combiner, integrating matching and load modulation in the output matching network of the main and peak PAs. To achieve high efficiency operation of the DPA at 7 dB output power back-off (OBO), an asymmetric 2.5:1 input power division ratio was realized. The DPA is operating at Ka-band between 25.5 and 27 GHz supporting two 750 MHz wide channels. Two digitally controlled phase shifters are implemented in the input of the main and peak PAs allowing on-chip phase balance of the main and peak signals. This allows for optimization of the performance across the two sub-bands. The DPA delivers a maximum saturated output power over 39.5 dBm at 24% PAE and over 17% PAE at 7 dB back-off operation.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband mmW Digital Step Attenuator
abstract: In this paper, we describe the design, analysis and evaluation of an ultra-wideband distributed-type digital step attenuator (DSA) covering most of the mmW frequency bands (between 40 and 220 GHz). Based on Fraunhofer IAF’s 35-nm mHEMT technology, we compare various approaches to realizing the unit cell (UC) of a distributed DSA. By using a tapered-stack topology, we minimize the circuit’s insertion loss and improve manufacturability. The fabricated 20-UC DSA features an attenuation depth of between 12.5 dB at 40 GHz and 23.5 dB at 220 GHz with a total of 11 steps. At the same time, its return loss above 40 GHz is better than 10 dB for all states. With these figures, this is the most broadband DSA published to date.

articleTitle: A 100W High Efficiency Hybrid Broadband GaN Power Amplifier for Galileo Navigation System
abstract: This paper presents the design and experimental characterization of a broadband hybrid high power amplifier (HPA) for L-band applications. The HPA has been optimized to work efficiently in the three sub-bands (E5, E6 and E1) dedicated to Galileo navigation system $(\mathrm{f}=1192 \pm 46 \mathrm{MHz}, \mathrm{f}=1278 \pm 25 \mathrm{MHz}$ and $f=1575 \pm 25 \mathrm{MHz}$, respectively), showing promising results. The HPA exploits a hermetic packaged device with an active periphery of 25.4 mm, developed in the $0.5 \mu \mathrm{m}$ gate length GaN/SiC HEMT process (GH50-20) available at United Monolithic Semiconductor (UMS) foundry. Experimental results shown output power even larger than 100 W with associated power added efficiency and gain of 60% and 14 dB, in more than a 35% of fractional bandwidth in L-Band. Indeed, the realized HPA shows very flat performance all along the frequency range from 1.14 GHz to 1.6 GHz, also achieving a quite good agreement between measurements and simulations.
